public_rationale: Two of the three parts hold. CNBC confirmed OpenAI expected about a $5 billion loss in 2024, so the business was losing money. OpenAI's own GPT-4.5 system card, published days before the post, shows its newest model still hallucinating on 19% of PersonQA questions, and says more work is needed. The third part, 'no sign of getting meaningfully better or more reliable', does not hold. The same system card shows the hallucination rate falling from 0.30 for GPT-4o to 0.19, and accuracy rising from 0.50 to 0.78. OpenAI described the release as having reduced hallucinations and more reliability. In December 2024 the independent ARC Prize team measured o3 at 75.7% on ARC-AGI-1 against 5% for GPT-4o, and called it a step-function increase. Whether these gains are 'meaningful' is a judgment call, but published signs of improvement did exist.
limitations: The loss figure is a press-reported projection, not audited results.
The hallucination numbers come from OpenAI's own evaluations.
The o3 ARC result was for a preview model tuned on ARC training data.

statement.excerpt: In simpler terms, SoftBank is investing as much as $25 billion in OpenAI, then spending another $3 billion a year on software that only loses money, and still hallucinates, and shows no sign of getting meaningfully better or more reliable.

from_speaker: "shows no sign of getting meaningfully better or more reliable"
subject: OpenAI's technology that SoftBank is paying for
our_interpretation: This is a three-part description of OpenAI's software as of the post date (2025-03-03).
'Only loses money': the plain reading is that OpenAI's business built on this software runs at a loss. The latest period public reporting could cover before the post is calendar 2024.
'Still hallucinates': OpenAI's current models still make up false facts at a measurable rate.

'No sign of getting meaningfully better or more reliable': the plain reading is that models released or evaluated in the period before the post showed no meaningful gains in capability or reliability (for example, hallucination rates) over earlier OpenAI models.
Target period: 2024-01-01 to 2025-03-03. That is the latest full reported year for finances, plus models and evaluations public by the post date. This choice is mine, because he named no period.
criteria.support_condition: All three parts hold: OpenAI lost money in the latest reported period; its models still hallucinate measurably; and evaluations up to the post date show no meaningful improvement in capability or reliability.
criteria.contradiction_condition: OpenAI was profitable, or its models did not measurably hallucinate, or published evaluations by the post date showed clear, meaningful gains in capability or reliability (such as lower hallucination rates or large benchmark jumps).
